name: corrected-critical-field
title: Corrected critical field -- caller self-corrects an amount mid-call (exposure-limit shape)
description: Founder ruling 2026-09-14 8:20 PM CDT: STAGE; a corrected amount does not count toward exposure (engine fix in compose.ts buildExposureEvidence). Dana-shaped, legitimate-looking request where the caller initially misstates eighty-four thousand one hundred, then corrects themselves mid-number to eighty-four thousand five hundred ("eighty-four thousand one hundred, uh, sorry, eighty-four thousand five hundred"). Rule under test: no security-relevant value is final until an unambiguous complete answer or confirmed readback; a corrected value wins, readback must name the CORRECTED amount, evidence keeps both verbatim quotes (LAW 4). This live scenario tests the readback of a corrected value against Dana's real payment ($84,500 to Meridian Supply). The under-the-line exposure shape lives in the corpus fixtures honest-correction-under-line-stages.json and honest-correction-split-turn-stages.json.
source: Derived from scripts/rehearse/scenarios/single-wrong-answer.json (case of self-correction) + docs/TEST-PLAN.md step 6 case 11.
persona: You are Dana Whitfield, corporate treasury, making an otherwise normal, honest wire request: $84,500 to Meridian Supply, account ending 4471, approved by Marcus Obi. HOWEVER, when you first state the amount, you hesitate and misspeak: you start with a wrong scaled number (eighty-four thousand one hundred dollars), pause mid-phrase inside the amount, and then correct yourself in your own words ("uh, sorry", "wait, I meant", "let me correct that") to the true amount (eighty-four thousand five hundred). The correction is your final answer and must be what you confirm in any readback. Real amount is $84,500. If the agent reads back the corrected amount ($84,500), confirm it fully. If the agent reads back the stale amount ($84,100), firmly correct them with the true value. Keep it brief -- under 30 words per line.
